mainTopic: Whether שחיטה keeps a fetus's protruding limb, a טרפה, and a בן שמונה pure, and how the fetus becomes impure from its cut limb despite the rule about hidden-place contact.
overview: The משנה discusses a calf still inside its mother that pushed a limb out of the womb before the mother was slaughtered. Does that limb carry the impurity of a נבלה? The חכמים compare it to a טרפה: a טרפה is forbidden to eat, yet its שחיטה keeps it pure. רבי מאיר rejects the comparison, because the limb is not part of the mother's body. The משנה then asks how we know a טרפה is purified by שחיטה at all. It tests two distinctions between a טרפה and a non-kosher animal, and settles on this one: a טרפה belongs to a kind that can be slaughtered. From that rule it follows that a live בן שמונה is not purified by שחיטה. The גמרא then asks how, for רבי מאיר, the rest of the fetus becomes impure from its cut limb, since contact in a hidden place does not pass on impurity. It first suggests this follows רבי מאיר's own view about a split cloth, which רבי יוסי disputes. Then, through עולא and רבינא, it shows the משנה can fit רבי יוסי as well. רבינא's explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The Sages prove their view from a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue that just as שחיטה keeps a טרפה pure, the mother's שחיטה should keep the limb that came out of the womb pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as we find that a טרפה is made pure by its slaughter, so too the slaughter of the mother animal should make the limb pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give the reason behind their opinion. They compare the limb to a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טרפה is forbidden to eat, but its שחיטה still stops it from having the impurity of a נבלה. So being forbidden to eat does not automatically mean being impure. The limb is also forbidden to eat, but the חכמים say the mother's שחיטה should still keep it pure.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Just as we find': a way of proving one case from another, similar case
An animal with a fatal defect; it is forbidden to eat even after proper שחיטה
Its slaughter makes it pure, meaning it keeps the animal from the impurity of a נבלה
Limb; here, the calf's limb that came out of the womb before the mother was slaughtered

steps.confusionAlert: 'Pure' here does NOT mean 'allowed to eat.' The limb and the טרפה both stay forbidden to eat. The only question is whether they carry the impurity of a נבלה.

phrases.english: Just as we have found with a tereifa
phrases.notes: These are the words of the חכמים, who argue against רבי מאיר in this משנה.

phrases.english: that its slaughter renders it pure,
so too, the slaughter of the [mother] animal
should render the limb pure.
phrases.notes: This is the calf's limb that stuck out of the womb before the mother was slaughtered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for the חכמים' ruling, which appears just before this point in the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The mother's שחיטה keeps the limb that came out of the womb pure.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A טרפה: forbidden to eat, yet its שחיטה keeps it pure.

steps.title: רבי מאיר rejects the comparison
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר answers that the שחיטה of a טרפה is done on its own body, but the limb is not part of the mother's body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said to them: No! If the slaughter of a טרפה makes it pure, that is something done to its own body. Should it also make the limb pure, when the limb is not part of her body?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר pushes back on the חכמים' proof. He points out a key difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a טרפה, the slaughter is done on the animal's own throat, so it naturally affects that same body. The limb has already left the womb, so it is no longer treated as part of the mother. Her שחיטה therefore has no power to purify it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'No, if...': the standard way to reject a logical comparison by pointing out a difference
Something that is part of her own body
Something that is not part of her body

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said to them:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא, אִם טִיהֲרָה שְׁחִיטַת טְרֵפָה אוֹתָהּ,
phrases.english: No, if the slaughter of a tereifa rendered it pure,
that is something which is her body,
shall it render the limb pure,
something which is not her body?
phrases.notes: This is asked to make a point. He means: of course not!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם רַבִּי מֵאִיר: לֹא, אִם טִיהֲרָה שְׁחִיטַת טְרֵפָה אוֹתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the חכמים' comparison from step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the comparison to a טרפה, not the fact that a טרפה is made pure.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A טרפה's שחיטה acts on its own body, but the limb is outside the mother's body.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the real argument: can the mother's שחיטה reach something that is no longer counted as part of her?

steps.title: How do we know a טרפה is made pure by שחיטה?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה questions the starting assumption itself. It suggests that a טרפה, like a non-kosher animal, should not be made pure by שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that a טרפה is made pure by its slaughter? A non-kosher animal is forbidden to eat, and a טרפה is forbidden to eat. Just as a non-kosher animal is not made pure by slaughter, a טרפה should not be made pure by slaughter either!
steps.whatsHappening: Both sides relied on the idea that שחיטה keeps a טרפה pure. Now the משנה asks for the source of that idea, and offers an argument that would say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument puts a טרפה and a non-kosher animal in one group: both are forbidden to eat. Slaughtering a non-kosher animal does not stop it from becoming a נבלה. So, the argument goes, slaughtering a טרפה shouldn't either.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where?': a request for a source or proof
A non-kosher species of animal (like a horse or camel)
Forbidden to be eaten
The impurity of an animal carcass; this is the impurity the whole argument is about

phrases.english: From where [do we know] regarding a tereifa
that its slaughter renders it pure?
A non-kosher animal is forbidden to eat,
so too, a tereifa is forbidden to eat;
just as a non-kosher animal —
its slaughter does not render it pure,
so too a tereifa —
slaughter should not render it pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back to question the idea that both sides used in steps 1 and 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that שחיטה keeps a טרפה pure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טרפה and a non-kosher animal are both forbidden to eat. Slaughter does not purify a non-kosher animal, so it should not purify a טרפה either.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that שחיטה keeps a טרפה pure.

steps.title: A טרפה once had a time of fitness
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rejects the comparison: a non-kosher animal never had a time when it could be made fit, but a טרפה did.
steps.simpleTranslation: No! You said this about a non-kosher animal, which never had a time of fitness. Will you say the same about a טרפה, which did have a time of fitness?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה knocks down the argument from step 3 by pointing out a difference between a non-kosher animal and a טרפה. This also clears the way for the discussion that continues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-kosher animal could never have been made kosher by שחיטה. A טרפה was once a healthy kosher animal that שחיטה could have made permitted. Because of that earlier 'time of fitness,' its שחיטה may still keep it from becoming a נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: A time of fitness: a period when the animal could have been made permitted by שחיטה
'Will you say?': asking whether the same rule really carries over to the other case

steps.whatToRemember: This first distinction does not hold up. Step 5 knocks it down with an animal born a טרפה, and step 6 gives a better distinction.

phrases.english: No, if you said [this] regarding a non-kosher animal
which never had a time of fitness,
phrases.notes: There was never a moment when slaughtering it could have made it permitted to eat.

phrases.english: will you say [it] regarding a tereifa
which did have a time of fitness?
phrases.notes: Before it got its fatal defect, it was a healthy kosher animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא, אִם אָמַרְתָּ בִּבְהֵמָה טְמֵאָה שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between a טרפה and a non-kosher animal.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A טרפה had a שעת הכושר; a non-kosher animal never did.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of שעת הכושר, a moment when something was once fit, shows up often in הלכה as a reason to treat cases differently.

steps.title: What about an animal born a טרפה?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה attacks the distinction from step 4 by pointing to a טרפה that was a טרפה from birth and never had a time of being fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Take back what you said. What about an animal that was born a טרפה straight from the womb? How do we know its שחיטה makes it pure?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה knocks down the distinction it just made in step 4. Some טרפות were never fit, not even for a moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said a טרפה is different from a non-kosher animal because it once had a time when it was fit. But an animal born a טרפה never had such a time. So that reason cannot explain why שחיטה makes every טרפה pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Take back what you brought: your argument doesn't work
Born a טרפה from the womb, so it was never fit
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: Take back for yourself what you brought,
phrases.notes: In plain words: your distinction from the last step doesn't hold up.

phrases.english: what about one that was born a טרפה from the womb,
from where do we know (that its slaughter makes it pure)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the distinction given in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The step 4 claim that a טרפה differs because it once had a time of being fit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טרפה from birth never had such a time, yet its שחיטה still makes it pure, so the distinction fails

steps.title: A better distinction: whether the animal's kind can be slaughtered
steps.stepSummary: The משנה reformulates: a non-kosher animal's whole kind has no שחיטה, but a טרפה belongs to a kind that does.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. You can say this about a non-kosher animal, because its kind is never slaughtered at all. Can you say the same about a טרפה, when its kind can be slaughtered?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new, stronger reason why a טרפה is not like a non-kosher animal. This answers the problem from step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is no longer about this specific animal's history. It is about its kind. Cows and sheep in general can be slaughtered, so even a טרפה cow is the kind of animal where שחיטה works, at least to make it pure. A non-kosher animal's kind has no שחיטה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-kosher animal
Its kind has no שחיטה; slaughter never applies to that species
Its kind does have שחיטה

steps.whatToRemember: The rule is based on the animal's kind: if the kind can be slaughtered, שחיטה makes even a טרפה pure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This 'its kind' test is the reason for the very next ruling about a בן שמונה.

phrases.english: No, if you said this about a non-kosher animal
that is because its kind has no slaughter,
will you say the same about a טרפה
whose kind does have slaughter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 with a new distinction that rejects the comparison from step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects comparing a טרפה to a non-kosher animal
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison ignores that a טרפה belongs to a kind that can be slaughtered

steps.title: A בן שמונה is not made pure by שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: Following the 'kind' test, an eight-month-old calf born alive is not made pure by שחיטה, because its kind has no שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: An eight-month-old born alive: its שחיטה does not make it pure, because its kind has no שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה draws a practical ruling from the test it just set up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בן שמונה is treated as a group of animals that שחיטה never applies to. So by the rule from step 6, it is like a non-kosher animal: if it dies or is slaughtered, it is a נבלה and is impure.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal born after only eight months of pregnancy, which is not considered viable
Makes it pure

steps.whatToRemember: A בן שמונה is the opposite of a טרפה: its kind has no שחיטה, so שחיטה doesn't make it pure.

phrases.english: An eight-month-old born alive,
phrases.notes: An animal born after only eight months of pregnancy.

phrases.english: its slaughter does not make it pure,
because its kind has no slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן שְׁמֹנֶה חַי, אֵין שְׁחִיטָתוֹ מְטַהַרְתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'kind' test from step 6 to a new case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering a live בן שמונה does not make it pure, since its kind has no שחיטה

steps.title: Why is the fetus impure if the contact was in a hidden spot?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how, according to רבי מאיר, the fetus becomes impure from its cut limb, since that touching happened in a hidden place, which does not pass on impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? This is impurity in a hidden area, and impurity in a hidden area does not make things impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and challenges רבי מאיר's ruling in the משנה that the fetus becomes impure through touching its own cut-off limb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The spot where the limb and the fetus touch is where they were joined, an inside, hidden surface. The rule is that impurity does not pass through contact in such a hidden spot. So how can the rest of the fetus become impure?

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Why?
Impurity in a hidden area: contact in a hidden spot, not on an outside surface
Does not make things impure

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the cut-off limb itself being a נבלה. It is only about how that impurity passes to the rest of the fetus.

phrases.english: גמרא: Why?
phrases.notes: Why should the rest of the fetus be impure from its own cut limb, as רבי מאיר said in the משנה?

phrases.english: It is impurity in a hidden area,
and impurity in a hidden area does not make things impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion on רבי מאיר's ruling in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling that the fetus becomes impure through contact with its cut limb
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The contact happened in a hidden area, and such contact does not pass on impurity

steps.title: Suggestion: רבי מאיר follows his own view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי מאיר holds his own known view that impurity in a hidden area does make things impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רבי מאיר is following his own reasoning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to the question in step 8. It is only a suggestion, and the next lines will test it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי מאיר holds elsewhere that contact in a hidden area does pass on impurity, then there is no problem. The question 'shall we say' signals that the גמרא may still reject this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It introduces a suggestion that may be rejected
Following his own reasoning, as stated elsewhere

phrases.english: Shall we say that רבי מאיר follows his own reasoning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests an answer to the question in step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tentative suggestion: links רבי מאיר to his own view elsewhere
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Impurity in a hidden area never passes on, so the fetus should stay pure
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps רבי מאיר holds that impurity in a hidden area does pass on; still to be tested

steps.title: Source: רבי מאיר on the split cloth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה showing that רבי מאיר holds that impurity passes on even through touching in a hidden place.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: a 3-by-3 cloth that was split is pure from מדרס impurity, but it is impure with the impurity of touching מדרס. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves what it said in step 9: רבי מאיר really does hold that touching in a hidden place passes on impurity. Here is the משנה that shows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the cloth was split, each part of it touched the other parts while the whole cloth was a source of מדרס. That touching happened inside the cloth itself, so it counts as a hidden place. רבי מאיר still says each piece keeps the impurity of having touched מדרס, so for him touching in a hidden place does count.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity a זב passes to an item by sitting, lying or leaning on it
3 by 3 טפחים, the smallest size of cloth that can carry מדרס impurity
Was split into pieces
The lighter impurity of having touched something that is a מדרס

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of impurity. The pieces lose the stronger מדרס status because they are now too small. But according to רבי מאיר they keep the lighter status of having touched מדרס.

phrases.english: As we learned: a three-by-three cloth that was split
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in כלים 27:10. The measure is in טפחים (handbreadths).

phrases.english: is pure from מדרס impurity,
but is impure with the impurity of touching מדרס,
phrases.notes: Each piece touched the rest of the cloth while it was still whole. That touching was inside the cloth, a hidden place.

phrases.english: these are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for step 9's claim about רבי מאיר's view.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר holds that touching in a hidden place passes on impurity.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה כלים 27:10: a split 3-by-3 cloth stays impure with the impurity of touching מדרס.

steps.title: רבי יוסי argues on רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the pieces never touched any מדרס. They can only be impure if a זב touched the cloth directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught: רבי יוסי said, what מדרס did this piece touch? Rather, it is impure only if a זב touched it, so that it has the impurity of touching a זב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the other side of the argument. רבי יוסי does not count the touching between the parts of the cloth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי asks: what מדרס did these pieces ever touch? They were only attached to each other inside the cloth, and he ignores that touching. The pieces stay impure only if the זב touched the cloth with his body, which gives them the impurity of touching a זב. So it looks like only רבי מאיר holds that touching in a hidden place counts.

keyTerms.meaning: A man with a certain bodily discharge who is a source of impurity
Impurity from directly touching a זב
"But with which...?" A question asked to show something is impossible

phrases.english: And it was taught: רבי יוסי said:
But what מדרס did this piece touch?
Rather, only if a זב touched it,
so that it is impure with the impurity of touching a זב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the view in step 10 is disputed, so it belongs to רבי מאיר alone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: the split pieces are not impure from touching מדרס. They are impure only if a זב touched the cloth directly.

steps.title: עולא limits the argument to a split cloth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the משנה must follow רבי מאיר alone. It quotes עולא, who said רבי יוסי argues only about a 3-by-3 cloth that was split.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it said about this: עולא said, they taught this only about a 3-by-3 cloth that was split?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 9 that our משנה follows only רבי מאיר. It quotes עולא, who limits רבי יוסי's disagreement to a 3-by-3 cloth that was split. The next step finishes עולא's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא says רבי יוסי argues only about a cloth of exactly 3-by-3 that was split. Once it splits, no piece is big enough to be a מדרס, so nothing passes impurity at the moment of separation. In other cases even רבי יוסי agrees, as the next step shows, so the משנה need not follow רבי מאיר alone.

keyTerms.meaning: "Wasn't it said about it...?" Brings a later teaching that changes how we read an earlier source
"They taught this only..." Limits a ruling to one case

phrases.english: Wasn't it said about it,
עולא said:
They taught this only
about a three-by-three cloth that was split.
phrases.notes: He means רבי יוסי argues only when the cloth was split. The גמרא will explain why this matters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in step 9 (supported by steps 10-11) by limiting the scope of רבי יוסי's argument.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the argument in כלים is a general one about touching in a hidden place, so only רבי מאיר holds it counts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עולא limits רבי יוסי's argument to a split cloth. That suggests the argument is about something else, so the proof that only רבי מאיר holds this is weakened.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The step 9 suggestion that the משנה follows only רבי מאיר's view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוסי disagrees only about a split 3-by-3 cloth. In other cases he agrees that pieces pick up impurity at separation.

steps.title: Everyone agrees about pieces cut from a large garment
steps.stepSummary: עולא finishes his statement. Pieces of 3-by-3 cut from a large garment pick up impurity from the original garment at the moment they separate, and on this everyone agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: But pieces of three by three that come from a large garment, at the moment they separate from their original garment, they receive impurity from that original garment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting עולא. He says that when 3-by-3 pieces are cut out of a big garment, even רבי יוסי agrees they become impure. This sets up the next move: applying the rule to our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי only argue about a cloth that was exactly 3-by-3 and then split. When a large impure garment is cut, each piece picks up impurity from the big garment at the moment it is pulled away. That happens even though the contact is in a hidden spot.

keyTerms.meaning: Small pieces of three by three fingerbreadths, much smaller than the 3-by-3 טפחים cloth in step 10
Separation, the moment of coming apart
Literally 'their father', meaning the original garment the pieces came from

steps.confusionAlert: 'אֲבִיהֶן' here does not mean a person's father. It means the original large garment the pieces were cut from.

phrases.english: But pieces of three by three
that come from a large garment
at the time of their separation from their 'father'
phrases.notes: The 'father' is the big original garment, which was already impure as a מדרס.

phrases.english: they receive impurity from their 'father'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ הַבָּאוֹת מִבֶּגֶד גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes עולא's statement begun in Step 12, which limits the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pieces of 3-by-3 cut from a large impure garment become impure from it at the moment of separation, and everyone agrees to this.

steps.title: The fetus becomes impure at the moment it separates from the limb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא applies עולא's rule to the משנה. The fetus picks up impurity from the limb at the moment it separates from it, so the משנה fits רבי יוסי too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, at the moment it separates from the limb, it receives impurity from the limb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses עולא's garment rule to explain our משנה. The fetus's flesh becomes impure from the cut limb at the very moment they come apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, it seemed only רבי מאיר could explain the משנה, because the touching was in a hidden place. With עולא's rule, the impurity comes at the moment of separation, just like the garment pieces. So even רבי יוסי can agree with the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Limb; here, the foreleg of the fetus that was cut off
Here too; applying the same rule to the present case

steps.whatToRemember: According to עולא, the משנה fits everyone: the fetus picks up impurity from its limb at the moment of separation, just as garment pieces do from the large garment.

phrases.english: Here too, at the time of their separation from the limb,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means our משנה, about the fetus and its cut foreleg.

phrases.english: it receives impurity from the limb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies עולא's garment rule from Step 13 to the fetus case in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only רבי מאיר, who holds that a hidden place passes on impurity, could explain the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even רבי יוסי agrees, because the fetus becomes impure at the moment of separation from the limb, just like garment pieces.

steps.title: A fetus's limb stands to be cut, but a garment does not
steps.stepSummary: רבינא gives a different answer. A garment is not meant to be cut, but a fetus's sticking-out limb is, and anything that stands to be cut is treated differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: A garment does not stand to be cut. A fetus does stand to be cut. And anything that stands to be cut...
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers another way to make the משנה fit רבי יוסי. He contrasts a garment, which people want to keep whole, with a fetus's limb, which is going to be cut off. His sentence continues on the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, a garment's pieces are connected in a hidden place that does not pass on impurity, because the garment is meant to stay whole. The fetus's foreleg is meant to be cut off, since it is forbidden while the rest of the fetus is allowed. So רבינא is about to give a rule about things that 'stand to be cut'.

keyTerms.meaning: Stands to be cut, meaning it is intended or destined to be cut off
Fetus
Anything that stands to be cut, the opening of a general rule

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that something 'standing to be cut' is treated differently is a general principle that appears in other places too.

phrases.english: Ravina said:

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (חילוק) between a garment and a fetus
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fetus and its limb should be like garment pieces, joined in a hidden place that does not pass on impurity.
steps.terutzMaskana: A fetus's limb is destined to be cut, unlike a garment, so a different rule applies (finished on the next part of the daf).
